# Fork vendor copy — semantica-agi/semantica (this file is fork-local)

> **Source of record:** this directory is a **git subtree import** of
> `https://github.com/semantica-agi/semantica.git` pinned to the `v0.6.6` tag.
> The actual upstream commit SHA is stamped in [`.upstream-version`](./.upstream-version)
> (regenerated on every `git subtree pull`).

## Why this directory exists

The multica fork integrates Semantica as a Labs flag (`semantica` in
`server/internal/experimental/catalog.go:367`) — the desktop main process
spawns the Semantica Explorer FastAPI server on a free loopback port and
Multica's reverse proxy mounts it at `/experimental/semantica/api/*`.

Pre-0.5.52 the integration depended on the **user's local clone** of
`semantica-agi/semantica` plus `pip install -e $SEMANTICA_REPO_PATH` — which
broke on:
- cold installs with no Python packaging tooling
- CI agents with no outbound network
- snapshot/clone rebuilds
- a future rename / archival of the upstream repo

The 0.5.52 Phase-0 port replaces that external dependency with this
**vendored subtree**. After `pnpm --filter @multica/desktop bundle-cli`,
`apps/desktop/resources/semantica/` mirrors this directory and `run.sh`
installs the prebuilt wheel from `builds/`.

## How to pull upstream updates

```bash
# Default: pin to a release tag
SEMANTICA_PIN=v0.6.7 bash scripts/sync-semantica-upstream.sh

# Or: follow main
SEMANTICA_PIN=main bash scripts/sync-semantica-upstream.sh
```

The script wraps `git subtree pull --squash` + `python -m build --wheel`
+ optional `bundle-cli`. See [`.omc/plans/semantica-research-and-porting-design.md`](../../../../../omc/plans/semantica-research-and-porting-design.md)
for the full design.

## How to keep fork-specific changes from clobbering on `subtree pull`

Any patch the fork needs that **upstream has not yet accepted** goes into
[`.fork-patches/`](./.fork-patches/) (empty at first import). The runtime
applies patches on `run.sh` startup via `git apply` — *not* by editing
files in `semantica/`, which is upstream tree and would conflict on the
next `subtree pull`.

When the patch is generic enough, file a PR upstream and delete the
fork-local copy.

## Local files (fork-only, NOT from upstream)

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `.upstream-version` | Single-line stamp: `<tag> @ <squashed-commit-sha>`. Auto-regenerated by `scripts/sync-semantica-upstream.sh`. |
| `README.fork.md` | This file. |
| `.gitattributes` | `linguist-vendored=true` so the GitHub language stats ignore this subtree. |
| `.fork-patches/` | Empty directory. Future fork-only patches land here. |

Everything else in this directory is upstream tree — do not edit.
